item.title: Pointfree convergence approach and pointfree index theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.05621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a category $\mathsf{C}$ of lattices, we introduce the category $\mathsf{C^{Cap}}$, a pointfree version of the category $\Cap$ of convergence approach spaces, that contains $\Cap$ coreflectively, as well as the category $\mathsf{C^{Conv}}$, of pointfree convergence spaces introduced by Goubault-Larrecq and Mynard, both reflectively and coreflectively. We investigate pointfree counterparts of pseudo-approach, pre-approach, and approach spaces along two natural axes---depth and adherence-determinedness---which coincide in the spatial case but diverge in general lattices, and we determine when the point--powerset adjunction restricts to these subcategories. Unlike in $\mathsf{C^{Conv}}$, the category $\mathsf{Ap}$ of approach spaces finds a natural analog $\mathsf{C^{Ap}}$ in $\mathsf{C^{Cap}}$ and "index theory" translating traditional topological or metric results into generalizing inequalities can be conducted. We illustrate this with a result involving measure of continuity and measure of compactness.
item.dc:creator: Emilio Angulo-Perkins, Fr\'ed\'eric Mynard

item.title: On Wilker-Type Properties
item.description: arXiv:2611.06060v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wilker-type properties record how a compact set can be split along a binary open cover, and they are precisely the continuity conditions for the union operation on open lattices, governing the topology of power and function spaces. We give a unified treatment of the four properties $\W$, $\Ww$, $\Wi$ and $\Win$. We prove that $\Wi$ and $\Win$ are hereditary for arbitrary subspaces, whereas $\W$ and $\Ww$ are hereditary only for closed subspaces; all four are preserved by continuous retracts, and $\Ww$, $\Wi$, $\Win$ are finitely additive over topological sums. For KC-spaces $\Ww$ and $\Wi$ coincide, and spaces whose compact subspaces are Hausdorff belong to $\Win$. Using Kov\'ar's compact KC-space $M_0$ and its variant $\QQ^{+}$, we obtain countably infinite compact KC-spaces in $\Wi\setminus\W$, showing $\Wi$ is strictly weaker than $\W$. Conversely, we construct compact $T_1$ spaces whose product fails $\Ww$, proving the classes $\Ww$ and $\Wi$ are not reflective. We further show Vietoris constructions need not preserve $\Wi$, and prove that $\Ok(M_0)\cong \Ck(M_0,\Sier)$ is not sober and fails property~$S$. Open problems are collected at the end.
item.dc:creator: Wu Wang, Jiajun Tang

item.title: Roughness of nets
item.description: arXiv:2611.06217v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce the concepts of ~`\emph{rough weighted ideal-$\tau$-convergence}' and ~`\emph{rough weighted ideal-$\tau$-cluster point}' of a net in locally solid Riesz spaces. We also compare these concepts with key findings from the works of Lahiri $\&$ Das (2007/2008), Das (2012) and Aytar (2008), as follows: [(i):] The set of \emph{ideal-cluster points} of a sequence in a topological space is closed, [(ii):] The set of \emph{ideal-cluster points} of a net in a topological space is closed, [(iii):] The set of \emph{rough ideal-cluster points} of a sequence in a norm linear space is closed. We demonstrate that, generally, the set of ~`\emph{rough weighted ideal-$\tau$-cluster points}' of a net in a locally solid Riesz space may not satisfy the aforementioned results, which implies that it may not be closed. This suggests that this set exhibits new characteristics, which we will discuss here. Ultimately, our characterization demonstrates that these new concepts can help identify an ideal that is maximal and effectively represent any closed $\tau$-neighborhood of $\theta$ within these spaces.
item.dc:creator: Sanjoy Ghosal, Mandobi Banerjee

item.title: A topological Mundici representation theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.05786v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We lift Mundici's equivalence between MV-algebras and abelian $\ell$-groups with a strong unit to the topological setting. To this end, we prove that, for every topological MV-algebra, the associated Mundici group can be endowed with a topology that extends the topology of the MV-algebra and makes it into an abelian topological $\ell$-group. Among such topologies there is a finest one; we identify this topology as the topological-group reflection of the bounded-stage final topology, and construct an explicit zero-neighbourhood base in terms of the original MV-algebra topology. Using this topology, we establish a topological Mundici adjunction that restricts to an equivalence between topological MV-algebras and Mundici-fine abelian topological $\ell$-groups with a strong unit. Here, Mundici-fine means that the group topology is the finest $\ell$-group extension of its unit-interval topology. We also identify extremal $\ell$-group extensions under additional hypotheses, and establish a quasitopological correspondence clarifying the distinction between separate and joint continuity.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Meng, Lili Shen, Dexue Zhang

item.title: A weak $\lambda$-set that is not a $\lambda$-set under $\frak{p} = \frak{c}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.06312v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Under $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak c$, Cantor space contains a weak $\lambda$-set that is not a $\lambda$-set. This answers the consistency question of de Oliveira Rodrigues, dos Santos Ronchim, and Szeptycki. The hypothesis $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak c$ is compatible with the failure of the continuum hypothesis. The construction combines the finite-unions form of Hindman's theorem with Bell's characterization of $\mathfrak p$ in terms of $\sigma$-centered forcing. The increasing enumerations of the infinite members of the constructed space form an unbounded family under eventual domination. This makes the countable set of finite subsets of $\omega$ a witness to the failure of the $\lambda$-property.
item.dc:creator: Alexander V. Osipov, Anton E. Lipin

item.title: $\sigma$-hereditarily closure-preserving $\mathcal I$-$sn$-networks, $\mathcal I$-$sn$-metrizability, and local HCP-finiteness
item.description: arXiv:2609.30317v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal I$ be an admissible ideal on $\mathbb N$. Zhou, Liu, Liu, and Lin asked whether every regular space with a $\sigma$-hereditarily closure-preserving $\mathcal I$-$sn$-network is $\mathcal I$-$sn$-metrizable. The answer is affirmative for every admissible ideal. The proof rests on a local countability theorem. If $y_n\to_{\mathcal I}x$ and $\{n\mid y_n\ne x\}\in\mathcal I^+$, then every point-discrete family of $\mathcal I$-sequential neighborhoods of $x$ is countable. In a $T_1$ space, this applies in particular to every HCP family. If no $\mathcal I$-convergent sequence to $x$ has $\mathcal I$-positive support away from $x$, then $\{x\}$ is an $\mathcal I$-sequential neighborhood. It follows that every space with a $\sigma$-point-discrete $\mathcal I$-$sn$-network is $\mathcal I$-$snf$-countable. This conclusion, together with the characterization theorems of Ge and of Zhou, Liu, Liu, and Lin, settles Problem 5.2. The countability bound cannot in general be strengthened to finiteness. A countable Rudin--Keisler antichain of free ultrafilters gives an admissible ideal for which local HCP-finiteness fails. Every $P^{-}$ ideal has local HCP-finiteness. Preservation theorems for Fubini products, heterogeneous Fubini sums under cross-row Kat\v{e}tov absorption, and suitable increasing unions extend local HCP-finiteness beyond the $P^{-}$ class. They apply to the finite Fubini powers of $\mathrm{Fin}$, Kat\v{e}tov's first limit-stage ideal $\mathrm{Fin}^{\omega}$ and its finite successors, the tree-derived rank-$\omega$ ideal $\mathcal H_{<\omega}$, and the inductive-limit ideal $\mathrm{Fin}_{\omega}$. Every listed example other than $\mathrm{Fin}$ fails $P^{-}$.
item.dc:creator: Xing-Yu Hu

item.title: Yet another approach to measuring distance in some hyperspaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.00249v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we define a new partial distance on hyperspaces consisting of closed balls, which is a partial metric in the sense of Matthews. We prove that these partial metric spaces are complete if and only if the metric spaces from which the corresponding ball spaces arise are complete. Finally, we compare the topology induced by the new partial distance with that induced by the classical Hausdorff distance.
item.dc:creator: Dariusz Bugajewski, Piotr Ma\'ckowiak

item.title: The topology of Gromov--Hausdorff space
item.description: arXiv:2609.09639v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the Gromov--Hausdorff space is homeomorphic to the real Hilbert space $\ell^2$. We construct a continuous assignment of full-support probability measures that is equivariant under isometries and finite-dimensional local approximations that control all pairwise distances. These approximations yield the absolute retract property for all metrizable spaces. We also prove that any countable family of continuous maps from compact metrizable spaces can be approximated, with respect to a prescribed open cover, by maps whose images form a discrete family.
item.dc:creator: Yoshito Ishiki

item.title: On the Complexity of Finding Fixed Points for Set-Valued Contractions
item.description: arXiv:2609.14101v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the computational complexity of finding fixed points of set-valued contractions. We first formulate a computational problem for Nadler's fixed-point theorem, PROJECTED-NADLER, and prove that it is CLS-complete by showing its equivalence to CONTINUOUS-LOCALOPT. We then establish a stronger converse to Nadler's theorem, which can be applied as a tool to analyze the convergence rate of the set-valued basic iteration procedure. Finally, we reduce the large-margin triplet stationarity problem to PROJECTED-NADLER. Combining the argument for CLS-hardness of exact triplet stationarity problem [Yan et al. 2025] with the CLS-hardness of approximate KKT points of quadratic programs [Fearnley et al. 2025], we obtain CLS-completeness of large-margin triplet stationarity at any prescribed accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Emmanouil-Vasileios Vlatakis-Gkaragkounis, Pucheng Xiong

item.title: Conway's thrackle conjecture: a new upper bound of $\frac43n$
item.description: arXiv:2610.31589v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A thrackle is a drawing of a graph in the plane in which every pair of edges meets exactly once, either at a common endpoint or at a proper crossing. Conway conjectured that every thrackle has at most as many edges as vertices. We give a short proof that every thrackle on $n\ge4$ vertices has at most $\lfloor4(n-1)/3\rfloor$ edges. The proof combines Pammer's computer-assisted verification of the conjecture for graphs on at most twelve vertices with a discharging argument in suitable plane and projective-plane embeddings. We also give bipartite plane graphs showing that the coefficient $4/3$ is best possible under the local hypotheses used in the proof.
item.dc:creator: D\'aniel G\'abor Simon
